1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and no cramped text, though letter spacing appears default rather than expanded.

2.why: No italics, all-caps prose, or dense paragraphs appear in any instruction; only the codes themselves are rendered in uppercase monospace.

3.why: Only a desktop viewport was captured, but the single-column ~560px card with large text and no wide tables should reflow readably to phone width.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short sentences in plain language (e.g., 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.'), with only occasional jargon such as 'authenticator' and 'MFA'.

5.why: The recovery-code field shows an example placeholder 'ABCD-EFGH-IJKL-MNPQ' and on-screen sample codes demonstrate the expected format, though the email and phone fields have no examples.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a two-sentence note, so the user never has to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as plain selectable text rather than images so they can be copied, but no explicit copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code is presented anywhere; step 3 explicitly offers manual secret entry only ('A QR code is not required'), so no QR alternative to manual entry exists.

9.why: The screenshots show only standard text inputs with no visible autofill affordances or any evidence of password-manager or OTP-autofill support.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the current step and a single high-contrast blue primary button that clearly stands out from secondary grey/red buttons.

11.why: Every screen requests a single primary action via one blue button, although step 1 collects two fields at once and the final screen adds secondary 'Generate new recovery codes' and 'Log out' options.

12.why: After actions the system states outcomes plainly ('Recovery code accepted. It cannot be used again.', 'MFA is active'), and each subsequent page explains what to do next.

13.why: A failed verification shows a retryable error with 'Start again' available, recovery codes can be regenerated, and code inputs are unmasked so entries are always visible, all with no observed lockout penalty.

14.why: The error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming and suggests a retry but does not state what the actual problem was (wrong versus expired code).

15.why: Pages can be read without a timer, but the verification code 'expires in five minutes' and authenticator codes rotate every 30 seconds, imposing time limits on code entry.
